set.rubric: per-scenario expect/track/severe/boundary/external inside the private set (unchanged)

models.sampling_source: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B@70d244cc README: non-thinking Temperature=0.7, TopP=0.8, TopK=20, MinP=0 (presence_penalty left at 0; the service uses 1.5)

alias: A packages the two models as P and Q and commits sha256(mapping JSON incl. random salt) before generation; mapping revealed only after C seals the judgment sha256
procedure: C generates P then Q sequentially, one model at a time, local Metal, isolated port, memory guard; live service untouched; AWS/external API 0
chat_blind_pack pack -> packet with per-scenario random 1/2 order; key file unopened
C judges all 500 user turns on the packet (verdict pass|partial|fail, severe codes, note)
C commits judgment sha256 (seal) in CHAT-BLIND-005-PROGRESS.md
unblind with key -> per-alias judgments; A reveals mapping+salt; C verifies commitment
sealed aggregator per model; final CHAT-BLIND-005.md
stop_rules: memory pressure or live service not running -> runner stops; the run is reported incomplete; a rerun needs supervisor approval
no per-question retry, no filtering, no output edits
blind_limits: C runs generation: the runner manifest records the model sha256 (both shas are already known to C), template tokens and sampling differ per model, so the alias is guessable before judging
the packet strips model/alias/file/timing fields, but answer style (length, markdown, emoji) can reveal the model
single AI judge (C); order key generated by C (procedural blind, not independent)
errata: reports/coordination/CHAT-EVAL-004/errata.jsonl rules unchanged: no criteria/threshold change after results; only verifiable C expected-value errors, reported both ways, gate uses the original
